quote.quote: The single biggest problem in communication is the illusion that it has taken place.
quote.author: George Bernard Shaw
quote.translation: 沟通中最大的问题，就是以为沟通已经发生了。
quote.explanation: 这句话提醒我们，仅仅发送信息并不等于有效沟通。在职场中，我们需要确认对方真正理解了我们的意思，避免想当然的假设。常用于反思会议、邮件或任务分配后的误解。

vocabulary.example: Our team needs to collaborate with the marketing department on the new campaign.
vocabulary.translation: 我们的团队需要和市场部合作开展新的推广活动。

vocabulary.example: She articulated her concerns about the project timeline during the meeting.
vocabulary.translation: 她在会议上清晰地表达了对项目时间表的担忧。

vocabulary.example: After hours of discussion, the team finally reached a consensus on the budget.
vocabulary.translation: 经过数小时的讨论，团队最终就预算达成了共识。

vocabulary.example: Please submit your report before the Friday deadline.
vocabulary.translation: 请在周五的截止日期前提交你的报告。

vocabulary.example: I appreciate your constructive feedback on my presentation.
vocabulary.translation: 我很感激你对我演示的 constructive 反馈。

vocabulary.example: We need to negotiate the terms of the contract with the client.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要与客户协商合同条款。

vocabulary.definition: 积极主动的；先发制人的
vocabulary.example: A proactive employee identifies potential problems before they become serious.
vocabulary.translation: 积极主动的员工会在潜在问题变得严重之前就发现它们。

vocabulary.example: Building rapport with colleagues is essential for effective teamwork.
vocabulary.translation: 与同事建立融洽关系对于有效的团队合作至关重要。

vocabulary.example: We must consider the needs of all stakeholders before making a decision.
vocabulary.translation: 在做出决定之前，我们必须考虑所有利益相关者的需求。

vocabulary.example: A concise email saves time and reduces the risk of miscommunication.
vocabulary.translation: 简洁的电子邮件可以节省时间并减少误解的风险。

pattern.example: Could you please elaborate on your proposed solution?
pattern.translation: 能否请您详细说明一下您提出的解决方案？
pattern.usage: 这是职场中非常礼貌的请求句型，用于请对方进一步解释或详细说明某个观点、计划或问题。适用于会议、邮件或一对一沟通中，既表示尊重又推动讨论深入。

grammar.title: 被动语态在正式沟通中的应用
grammar.explanation: 在职场书面或正式口头沟通中，被动语态（be + 过去分词）常用来淡化动作执行者，突出动作本身或结果，使语气更客观、礼貌。例如，当批评或指出问题时，使用被动语态可以避免直接指责某人。常用于会议记录、报告、邮件等。
examples: The deadline was missed due to unforeseen delays. （避免说“你错过了截止日期”，更客观）
A decision will be made after all stakeholders have been consulted. （突出决策过程而非决策者）

pronunciation.tips: 重音在第二个音节 /ˈtɪk/。注意 /r/ 要卷舌，/ɑː/ 是长元音，类似“啊”但更长。结尾 /leɪt/ 要清晰，不要吞掉 /t/。可以拆分：ar-tic-u-late。
examples: She is an articulate speaker who can convey complex ideas clearly.
He struggled to articulate his thoughts during the high-pressure interview.

reading.title: The Art of Clear Workplace Communication
reading.content: Effective communication is the backbone of any successful organization. It involves not only speaking clearly but also listening actively and choosing the right medium. In meetings, always state the purpose upfront and summarize key points at the end. When writing emails, use a descriptive subject line, keep paragraphs short, and avoid jargon unless your audience is familiar with it. Another crucial skill is asking clarifying questions instead of assuming. For example, instead of saying 'I understand,' ask 'Could you confirm that I’m on the right track?' Remember that non-verbal cues—like eye contact and nodding—can build rapport. Above all, be concise: respect others' time by delivering your message in the fewest words possible. By mastering these practices, you'll reduce misunderstandings, increase trust, and foster a collaborative environment.
reading.translation: 有效沟通是任何成功组织的基石。它不仅包括清晰表达，还包括积极倾听和选择合适的媒介。在会议中，始终先说明目的，并在结束时总结要点。写邮件时，使用描述性主题行，保持段落简短，除非听众熟悉，否则避免使用行话。另一个关键技能是提出澄清性问题，而不是凭空猜测。例如，不要只说“我明白了”，而要问“您能确认我的理解是正确的吗？”记住，非语言信号——比如眼神交流和点头——可以建立融洽关系。最重要的是，要简洁：用最少的词传达信息，尊重他人的时间。通过掌握这些实践，你将减少误解，增加信任，并营造协作的环境。
